title: Rabbi Oshaya son of Rabbi Shammai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: (Hyman places him as a Palestinian Amora of the fifth generation, in Caesarea.) His father Rabbi Shammai was the leading sage of the generation in the generation of Rabbi Yose, as explained in his entry, and Rabbi Oshaya was the leading sage of the generation in Rabbi Mana’s time, as in Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 3:2: “Rabbi Mana sent a letter to Rabbi Hoshaya son of Rabbi Shimi: ‘Though your beginning was small,’” etc. In Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 6:3: “Rabbi Mana said: I went to Caesarea and heard Rabbi Hoshaya bar Shimi in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar.” In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 11, end of halakhah 4, and Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 2:3: “Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Elazar instructed Rabbi Hoshaya son of Rabbi Shimi.” In Jerusalem Talmud Sotah, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, and Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:4 he disagrees with Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Bun.

He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 3:3. In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:4 it reads Rabbi Yehoshaya son of Rabbi Shammai, and Hyman proposes Rabbi Hoshaya. In Kohelet Rabbah 9:10, Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar called Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Timi and Rabbi Burki “the holy congregation”; Hyman suggests “Rabbi Oshaya son of Rabbi Shimi.”

notes.text: The chapter/halakhah chain is Jerusalem Talmud. The son Oshaya is the leading sage in Mana’s time; the father Shammai belongs to Yose’s generation. Shammai/Shimi/Timi and Hoshaya/Oshaya/Yehoshaya corrections remain Hyman’s, not a family merge.

The inspected Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 6:3 reads Hoshaya bar Shammai in Mana’s Caesarea report, where Hyman gives Shimi. The father/son generation argument and the Shammai/Shimi/Timi and Hoshaya/Yehoshaya emendations remain Hyman’s occurrence-specific account.
